=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh: Line or code reference: 102 (exit 0 at end of script); line 102; lines 98-102; 82-102; 102, `exit 0` (unconditional); entire script (102 lines) | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The helper returns status 0 on validation and credential-operation failures, so callers cannot detect failed hides or restores.
  WHY: Workflow steps and tests treat exit 0 as success; this finding is consistently rated BLOCKER, with z-ai_glm-5_2 also describing early-exit paths that omit expected diagnostics.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh: Line or code reference: 81, `if [[ "${url}" =~ ^https://github\.com/ ]]; then`; lines 81-83; 81-83; 81-82; 81-83, restore origin case | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Restore accepts any GitHub-hosted origin without verifying that the repository matches `GITHUB_REPOSITORY` or the trusted support repository.
  WHY: An editor-changed origin on github.com passes the host check and receives `GH_TOKEN`.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh: Line or code reference: lines 29-54, the entire hide action; lines 34-44 and lines 77-83; 35-53; 19-54 (hide) and 76-97 (restore) | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Hide and restore do not inspect or reject `remote.origin.pushurl` or `url.*.pushInsteadOf` overrides.
  WHY: Pushes can use an attacker-controlled destination or retain credentials despite the origin URL being cleaned; reviewers consistently rated this BLOCKER.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh: Line or code reference: 29-30, `repo_git "${repo}" rev-parse --git-dir`; line 30; 13-16,29-33 (hide repo iteration) and default repos list | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Checkout detection uses `git rev-parse --git-dir`, which discovers a parent repository when the supplied path is a non-git subdirectory.
  WHY: Hide can treat the parent as the checkout and strip its origin credentials.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh: lines 29-54, the entire hide action; 13-16,29-33 (hide repo iteration) and default repos list | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Hide does not require or validate `GITHUB_REPOSITORY` before stripping credentials.
  WHY: Without a trusted repository identity, hide cannot establish that the checkout is the workflow repository.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh: lines 76-83, the restore origin case; lines 81-83 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Restore does not reject multiple `remote.origin.url` entries.
  WHY: It can validate only one URL while another configured origin URL remains available as an attacker-controlled destination.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh: lines 85-93; lines 85-93; 85-92; 85-93, extraheader case; 85-93, extraheader case | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Restore reinstates extraheaders without scoping them to the verified origin repository.
  WHY: A host-wide or attacker-scoped authorization header can apply to unrelated GitHub repositories or leak `GH_TOKEN`.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh: Line or code reference: 39, `printf '%s\torigin\n' "${repo}" >> "${marker}"` | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: The marker does not record baseline origin URLs or extraheader keys for comparison during restore.
  WHY: Restore cannot detect same-host origin or extraheader drift from hide-time state.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh: lines 61-97, the restore loop; lines 61-97; 61-97, restore loop; 61-97, restore loop | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Restore injects credentials into checkouts as it processes the marker instead of validating every checkout first.
  WHY: If a later checkout fails validation, earlier checkouts already have `GH_TOKEN` written to their git configuration.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh: lines 62-75 and 85-93, extraheader without validated origin; lines 62-97; 61-97, restore loop | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Restore can process an extraheader marker entry without first validating an origin entry for that checkout.
  WHY: An authorization token can be injected into a checkout whose origin was never validated.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh: Line or code reference: 56, `[ -s "${marker}" ] || exit 0`; line 56; line 56; line 56, `[ -s "${marker}" ] || exit 0` | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Restore exits silently when the marker is missing or empty instead of emitting the expected `reason=marker_missing` diagnostic.
  WHY: Callers cannot distinguish a no-op restore from a successful restore; severity ratings disagree between BLOCKER and MAJOR, so the highest severity is retained.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh: lines 57-59, `if [ -z "${GH_TOKEN:-}" ]; then ... exit 0`; lines 57-60 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash]
  PROBLEM: Restore exits successfully when `GH_TOKEN` is missing.
  WHY: The checkout remains without restored Git credentials while the caller is told restoration succeeded.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh: Line or code reference: 21-23, the existing-marker check in hide; lines 21-24; 21-24, hide when marker exists | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Hide warns and exits successfully when an unrestored marker already exists.
  WHY: A subsequent editor launch can proceed without a fresh credential hide; severity ratings disagree between BLOCKER and MAJOR, so the highest severity is retained.
- .github/workflows/implement.yml: 2878-2879; 2727-2730, 2874-2900 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The workflow does not gate editor execution on successful credential hiding.
  WHY: Because hide failures return success, the editor can run while credentials remain exposed.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh: Line or code reference: 96, per-item outcome log in restore loop; lines 61-97 | severity=low | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: The per-item restore log uses cumulative `failed` state rather than the current item's outcome.
  WHY: After one item fails, later successful items are misreported as warnings.

=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: "The credential helper rejects failed hides/restores and restores auth only when the origin still names the workflow's original repository (or its trusted support checkout) and its push URL agrees, not an editor-changed GitHub destination; generic GitHub extraheaders are restored scoped to the verified origin only."
  expected_change_site: scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh — hide and restore actions
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  EVIDENCE: scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh does not validate the repository path against GITHUB_REPOSITORY; does not check or reject pushurl or pushInsteadOf rewrites; does not reject multiple remote.origin.url entries; does not scope restored extraheaders to the verified origin; does not validate all checkouts before injecting tokens; does not require a validated origin before accepting an extraheader entry; does not record a baseline URL/key set on hide for comparison on restore; and unconditionally exits 0. Evidence also includes test_restore_rejects_a_repo_name_matching_regex_punctuation at tests/test_heal_evidence_editor_isolation.py:82-93 and tests/test_heal_evidence_editor_isolation.py:82-91, plus 16 failures in tests/test_heal_evidence_editor_isolation.py.
- requirement: "Plan and implement receive only the bounded `diagnostics.json` structured prompt section; raw job and artifact files are not linked in those prompts, and free-form step names and error signatures are represented only by SHA-256 fingerprints."
  expected_change_site: scripts/workflow_failure_heal_evidence.py — `render_structured_prompt_section`
  confidence=[3]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  EVIDENCE: scripts/workflow_failure_heal_evidence.py:1185-1187 renders "Steps: unavailable" for non-list steps, while scripts/workflow_failure_heal_evidence.py:830-835 sets `job["steps"] = "unavailable"` for cached jobs; the reviewer says the cached-job path may not provide the per-step fingerprint lines expected by test_structured_legacy_cached_job_and_missing_data.
- requirement: PR description / README / agents.md: "Implement runs with heal evidence also pin the issue/plan file allowlist before the editor and block out-of-scope commits even when the normal guard or per-run override is disabled."
  expected_change_site: scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh; implement.yml scope-lock wiring; implement_commit_changes.sh
  confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [z-ai_glm-5_2]
  EVIDENCE: The scope-lock wiring is present at implement.yml:3410-3413,3659-3735,4351-4354 and implement_commit_changes.sh:478-552, but scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh unconditionally exits 0, so credential failure is not detected even though the scope lock can block commits.

=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh: Line or code reference: 102 (exit 0 at end of script) | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The script unconditionally exits 0 and never inspects the `failed` flag.
  WHY: Every caller treats validation failures as success, including cases where GH_TOKEN is injected into an attacker repository.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh: Line or code reference: 81, `if [[ "${url}" =~ ^https://github\.com/ ]]; then` | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Restore checks only the GitHub host, not whether repository identity matches `GITHUB_REPOSITORY` or the trusted support checkout.
  WHY: A same-host editor-changed repository passes validation and receives GH_TOKEN; the reviewer cites test_restore_rejects_a_repo_name_matching_regex_punctuation.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh: Line or code reference: lines 29-54, the entire hide action | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Hide does not validate `GITHUB_REPOSITORY`, inspect pushurl or pushInsteadOf overrides, or validate the origin path.
  WHY: Push traffic can be redirected to an attacker destination while credentials are hidden from origin; hide also proceeds without trusted repository identity.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh: Line or code reference: lines 76-83, the restore origin case | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Restore does not inspect pushurl, pushInsteadOf rewrites, or multiple origin URLs before injecting GH_TOKEN.
  WHY: A push override can send the restored token to an attacker-controlled destination.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh: Line or code reference: lines 85-93, the restore extraheader case | severity=critical | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Restore does no
